title: UK MP Dhesi Presses Punjab Officials on NRI Land Disputes and Air Connectivity
excerpt: British MP Tanmanjeet Singh Dhesi met Punjab's NRI affairs minister to push for a one-window grievance system, direct flights to Amritsar and Chandigarh, and reopening of the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor.
body:
• UK MP Tanmanjeet Singh Dhesi met Punjab NRI affairs minister Sanjeev Arora in Jalandhar to discuss land disputes, extortion calls targeting overseas Punjabis, and air connectivity gaps.
  • Dhesi pushed for an effective one-window system for NRI grievances and called for direct flights from London, Birmingham, and other global cities to Amritsar and Chandigarh.
  • The MP urged the reopening of the Amritsar International Cargo Port, closed after recent India-Pakistan tensions, and the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor.
  • Long-pending issues including the release of Sikh political prisoners and the case of British national Jagtar Singh Johal were also raised.

British MP Tanmanjeet Singh Dhesi met Punjab NRI affairs minister Sanjeev Arora in Jalandhar for an hour-long meeting that covered a wide range of issues affecting the Punjabi diaspora, from property seizures and extortion to aviation links and diplomatic matters.

Land Disputes and Extortion

The meeting focused heavily on land dispute and seizure matters, which remain among the most persistent grievances for Non-Resident Indians with roots in Punjab. Dhesi, who represents the Slough constituency in the UK Parliament, underlined that extortion calls targeting NRIs have become a growing safety concern and need urgent attention from state authorities.

To address these issues, Dhesi called for an effective one-window system that overseas Punjabis could rely on to resolve property disputes, protect their investments, and facilitate business ventures in the state, according to NewsPoint.

Pushing for Direct Flights

Dhesi highlighted the need for more direct flights to Amritsar and Chandigarh, particularly from London, Birmingham, and other European destinations, as well as North America and Asia. He argued that improved connectivity would help connect the global Punjabi diaspora directly with Punjab while boosting trade, tourism, and cargo activities.

"Given the millions of Punjabi diaspora, Punjab could emerge as a major power in the aviation sector."

— Tanmanjeet Singh Dhesi, UK Member of Parliament

The aviation push comes as the Punjab government under Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann has been working to expand the state's air connectivity, including efforts to resume domestic flights from the Adampur airport in Jalandhar and complete a civil air terminal at Halwara.

Diplomatic and Political Issues

The meeting also raised the status of the Amritsar International Cargo Port, which was closed following recent India-Pakistan tensions. Dhesi noted that its reopening would benefit both nations, with Punjabis standing to gain the most from restored cross-border trade.

The MP also requested pressure for reopening the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor, a key pilgrimage route for Sikhs worldwide. The corridor, which allows visa-free access to the Gurdwara Darbar Sahib Kartarpur in Pakistan, has been a sensitive diplomatic issue between the two countries.

Other long-pending issues discussed included the release of Sikh political prisoners who have served their sentences and the case of Jagtar Singh Johal, a British national detained in India since 2017. Dhesi expressed hope that the Punjab government and Indian authorities would take these matters seriously.

A Recurring Advocacy Pattern

Dhesi has long been among the most vocal UK parliamentarians on issues affecting the Punjabi diaspora. He has previously met with CM Mann to discuss NRI investment policies, land reform, and direct flight routes. In earlier visits, he lobbied Virgin Atlantic and Air India officials to consider launching direct flights between UK cities and Amritsar, citing the commercial potential of the route.

The MP has also advocated for dedicated NRI police stations, special fast-track courts for property disputes, and empowering Punjab's NRI Commission with executive authority beyond its current advisory role.

What's Next

Punjab officials have indicated willingness to work with Delhi on aviation permissions and with international carriers on new route scheduling. The state is also reviewing how to better brief district police and revenue officers on NRI cases to prevent the one-window system from stalling at the local level. For the millions of Punjabis abroad, the question remains whether these discussions will translate into concrete action on longstanding grievances.
nri_angle: Directly addresses NRI concerns including property disputes, extortion, and connectivity for the large UK-based Punjabi community.
